new_defects.title: /sitemap/5.xml introduced today but is empty (0 URLs)
new_defects.evidence: GET https://www.nakshiq.com/sitemap/5.xml returns 200, 111 bytes, an empty <urlset>. The top-level /sitemap.xml index added /sitemap/5.xml today, alongside the recovery from 500→200 on the index itself. Empty sitemap chunks are valid XML but waste a crawl request and may indicate an incomplete deploy or a placeholder for content that didn't ship.
new_defects.impact: Search-engine crawlers fetch the empty chunk on every crawl pass — small cost, but it's an unintentional surface. If the chunk is meant to hold something (e.g. blog/articles), the data wasn't generated.

new_defects.title: Destination → state route refactor: /en/destination/goa now 301-redirects to /en/state/goa
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/destination/goa returns 301 with Location: /en/state/goa. /en/state/goa returns 200, 278,555 bytes. Goa was a destination yesterday (in the cold-render perf panel; PRERENDER on 2026-04-29). Today it has been promoted/relocated to a state-level page. Spot-check confirms goa is the only /en/destination/<slug> in the 12-panel that newly redirects; jaipur, shimla, manali, panaji, munnar, varanasi, darjeeling, udaipur, leh, binsar, kaza, spiti all stay as destination pages.
new_defects.impact: Inbound deep links and any third-party SEO equity targeting /en/destination/goa lose one hop today, then recover via the 301. Risk: Google cache + LLM crawlers may need a few days to re-resolve. If more destinations get this treatment (especially top-traffic ones), monitor Search Console for 'soft 404' or 'page with redirect' bumps.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[slug]/page.tsx — confirm intended scope of the refactor and document the redirect map)

new_defects.impact: Bilingual SEO is leaving Hindi-page indexability on the table — Google has no signal that /en/destination/jaipur and /hi/destination/jaipur are alternates, so it may de-duplicate them or pick the wrong canonical.

new_defects.title: Soft-404 on /destination/<bad-slug> persists in BOTH locales (5th consecutive day)
new_defects.evidence: /en/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200, 73,611 bytes; /hi/destination/this-does-not-exist-xyz → 200, 84,329 bytes. Both serve homepage shell. /en/collections/<bad>, /en/region/<bad>, and /en/state/<bad> correctly return 404 — soft-404 is still isolated to the destination route group. Spiti (a slug listed in llms.txt with no canonical destination row) reproduces the same shell-200 in both locales.
new_defects.impact: Crawlers can index unbounded fake URLs; analytics gets dirtied; llms.txt 'destinations' list points at slugs that 200-but-don't-exist.
new_defects.recommended_owner: web (apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[slug]/page.tsx — call notFound() when the row is missing)

new_defects.title: Numeric month sub-routes /destination/<slug>/<1-12> still soft-404 (llms.txt contract violation)
new_defects.evidence: Probed /en/destination/jaipur/3, /5, /10 and /en/destination/shimla/3, /5, /10 — all returned 200 with 73,899-73,901 bytes (homepage shell). The named variants (/march, /may, /october) return 146-173KB real pages with proper titles ('Jaipur in March 2026: …'). llms.txt advertises numeric month routes; they are not honored. /hi/destination/jaipur/march returns 183KB real content (Hindi month route works).
new_defects.impact: AI crawlers following llms.txt advice get indexed onto homepage HTML for what they think are month-specific destination pages — bad for citation quality and llms.txt audits.

new_defects.title: /en/cost-index payload still 3.61MB (no shrink in 96h)
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/cost-index returned 200 in 2.308s with 3,613,301 bytes. Within 14 bytes of 2026-04-29 (3,613,315) and ~700 bytes of 2026-04-28 (3,612,641). 4 consecutive days with no shrink.
new_defects.impact: Slow load on mobile / 2 Mbps connections (≈15s download). Likely a large embedded data payload that should be paginated, code-split, or fetched async.

new_defects.title: Confidence mention count drops EXACTLY 2 in /hi vs /en across 8 destinations (5th day with same delta)
new_defects.evidence: Per-page count of literal token 'confidence' in HTML, en→hi: jaipur 11→9, shimla 12→10, manali 15→13, leh 13→11, varanasi 11→9, udaipur 9→7, darjeeling 9→7, kaza 8→6. Delta is consistently 2 — strongly suggests two specific 'confidence' UI strings remain English-only on /en pages while their /hi counterparts are localized to a different word (or absent). Identical to 2026-04-29.
new_defects.impact: Adds a deterministic data point under BUG-005 — the gap is a fixed two-string bug, not rolling content drift.
new_defects.reproduction: for s in jaipur shimla manali leh varanasi udaipur darjeeling kaza; do echo $s; for l in en hi; do curl -s https://www.nakshiq.com/$l/destination/$s | grep -oiE confidence | wc -l; done; done

new_defects.title: /en/regions index page still 404 (no redirect added with region→state refactor)
new_defects.evidence: GET /en/regions returns 404 / 27,436 bytes. Today's region→state route refactor moved /en/region/<slug> → 301 → /en/state/<slug> and introduced /en/states (308) → /en/state (200, 136KB index). The plural /en/regions URL was not updated; a 301 to /en/state would close the loop.
new_defects.impact: Any inbound link or older sitemap entry pointing at /en/regions hits a dead end instead of riding the refactor.

gaps: Cold-render performance is collected from whatever happens to be cache=MISS on probe; no controlled invalidation. Today's MISS set was darjeeling (en+hi), binsar (en+hi), ranthambore, lonavala, mahabaleshwar — different from yesterday's set, so day-over-day cold-render comparison is approximate.

Live console message capture is partial — Chrome MCP starts tracking only after the first read_console_messages call. BUG-012 verdict relies on a navigate-then-read pattern; only the chrome-extension messages were captured (6 entries), so any synchronous Supabase warnings emitted before navigation completed could be missed.

Browser-side performance metrics sampled on 3 page loads only (jaipur initial, manali reload, jaipur fresh-nav); primary perf signal remains curl time_total which conflates DNS+TLS+TTFB+download. Real-user TTFB / LCP / INP would require a full Web Vitals run.
/en/state index returns 200 + 136KB but I did not enumerate its child link count or compare against /en/regions historical state list. Recommend a state-route inventory test for the next run.
